name: Montelukast
route_note: Oral tablet, chewable tablet or granules once daily

discovery.by: Merck Frosst Centre for Therapeutic Research, Montreal
discovery.note: Optimised from earlier leukotriene D4 antagonists to allow once-daily oral dosing.

tagline: Once-daily oral leukotriene blocker for asthma and allergic rhinitis
summary: Montelukast is an oral antagonist of the cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptor. It is used as add-on or alternative controller therapy in asthma, for exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and for allergic rhinitis, and carries an FDA boxed warning about neuropsychiatric events.
mechanism: Cysteinyl leukotrienes (LTC4, LTD4, LTE4), released by mast cells and eosinophils, constrict airway smooth muscle, increase vascular permeability and mucus secretion, and recruit eosinophils.

Montelukast binds the CysLT1 receptor with high affinity and selectivity, blocking these effects. It is less effective than inhaled corticosteroids as a sole controller but works orally and is useful in aspirin-exacerbated and exercise-induced disease.
uses: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma
Seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (when other treatments are unsuitable)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Montelukast is identified at Merck Frosst in Canada.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Singulair is approved for asthma in adults and children aged 6 and older.

history.title: Allergic rhinitis
history.detail: Approval extended to seasonal allergic rhinitis.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: US patent exclusivity ends and generic montelukast launches.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning on serious neuropsychiatric events, including suicidal thoughts and actions, and advises against use for mild allergic rhinitis.

history.title: Organon spin-off
history.detail: Singulair moves to Organon when Merck spins off its established brands.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic, mainly CYP2C8, with CYP3A4 and CYP2C9

serious: Neuropsychiatric events (agitation, depression, sleep disturbance, suicidal thinking and behaviour)
Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (often on steroid withdrawal)
safety.boxed_warning: Serious neuropsychiatric events, including suicidal thoughts or actions; reserve for allergic rhinitis patients who respond inadequately to or cannot tolerate other therapies.

facts: Montelukast was among the world's best-selling asthma drugs before its patent expired in 2012.
Zafirlukast and pranlukast are related CysLT1 antagonists; zileuton instead inhibits 5-lipoxygenase.
